passed.title: Expr.list.get and Expr.list.gather raise on out-of-bounds indices by default
passed.trap: The `Expr.list.get` docstring prose says an out-of-bounds index returns `None`, but the default is `null_on_oob=False`, which raises an error. `Expr.list.gather` has the same default. A single empty or short sublist is enough to make the whole query fail. Pass `null_on_oob=True` when sublists can be shorter than the index. To take the first or last element, use `Expr.list.first` or `Expr.list.last`, which return null for empty lists.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[3, 2, 1], [], [1, 2]]})
try:
    df.select(pl.col("a").list.get(0))
except Exception as e:
    print(getattr(type(e), "__name__"))
try:
    df.select(pl.col("a").list.gather([0, 2]))
except Exception as e:
    print(getattr(type(e), "__name__"))
out = df.select(
    get=pl.col("a").list.get(0, null_on_oob=True),
    first=pl.col("a").list.first(),
    last=pl.col("a").list.last(),
    taken=pl.col("a").list.gather([0, 2], null_on_oob=True),
)
print(out.to_dict(as_series=False))

passed.title: Expr.list.len counts null elements
passed.trap: `Expr.list.len` returns the number of elements in each sublist, and null elements count toward that total. If you expect a count of non-null values, the result is silently too high. To count only non-null elements, drop the nulls first with `Expr.list.drop_nulls` and then call `Expr.list.len`.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[1, 2, None], [None], [5]]})
out = df.with_columns(
    len_with_nulls=pl.col("a").list.len(),
    non_null=pl.col("a").list.drop_nulls().list.len(),
)
print(out.to_dict(as_series=False))

passed.title: Expr.list.all is True and Expr.list.any is False for empty or all-null lists
passed.trap: When a row has no non-null elements, `Expr.list.all` returns `True` and `Expr.list.any` returns `False`. This applies to both `[]` and `[null]`, while a null list gives null. A filter such as "every check passed" therefore keeps rows that ran no checks at all. If an empty or all-null list should not count as passing, also require at least one non-null element.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[True], [False, True], [None], [], None]})
has_values = pl.col("a").list.drop_nulls().list.len() > 0
out = df.with_columns(
    naive_all=pl.col("a").list.all(),
    strict_all=pl.col("a").list.all() & has_values,
    any=pl.col("a").list.any(),
)
print(out.to_dict(as_series=False))
passed.output: {'a': [[True], [False, True], [None], [], None], 'naive_all': [True, False, True, True, None], 'strict_all': [True, False, False, False, None], 'any': [True, True, False, False, None]}

passed.title: Expr.list.join needs String elements and silently skips nulls
passed.trap: `Expr.list.join` errors if the list's inner type is not `String`. Cast first, for example with `Expr.cast(pl.List(pl.String))`. The default `ignore_nulls=True` silently drops null elements, so `[1, null, 3]` becomes `"1-3"` with no trace of the missing value. Pass `ignore_nulls=False` if a sublist containing a null should produce a null string.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[1, None, 3], [4, 5]]})
try:
    df.select(pl.col("a").list.join("-"))
except Exception as e:
    print(getattr(type(e), "__name__"))
s = pl.col("a").cast(pl.List(pl.String))
out = df.select(
    skip_nulls=s.list.join("-"),
    propagate=s.list.join("-", ignore_nulls=False),
)
print(out.to_dict(as_series=False))

passed.title: List set operations match nulls as values and do not sort the result
passed.trap: The list set operations treat null as an ordinary value. A null on both sides is removed by `Expr.list.set_difference` and kept by `Expr.list.set_intersection`. The output is not sorted, so `Expr.list.set_symmetric_difference` can return `[8, 5, 7]`. Do not compare results by position or against a sorted literal. Apply `Expr.list.sort` when order matters.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[None, 3], [5, 6, 7]], "b": [[3, 4, None], [6, 8]]})
out = df.with_columns(
    diff=pl.col("a").list.set_difference("b"),
    inter=pl.col("a").list.set_intersection("b"),
    sdiff=pl.col("b").list.set_symmetric_difference("a"),
    sdiff_sorted=pl.col("b").list.set_symmetric_difference("a").list.sort(),
)
print(out.to_dict(as_series=False))

passed.title: Use Expr.list.agg, not Expr.list.eval, to get a scalar per row
passed.trap: `Expr.list.eval` does not automatically explode its result. An aggregation such as `pl.element().null_count()` inside it therefore returns a `List(UInt32)` column of one-element lists like `[[1], [0], [2]]` instead of a scalar column. Use `Expr.list.agg` when you want one scalar per row, because it automatically explodes the aggregated result and yields a plain `UInt32` column.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[1, None], [42, 13], [None, None]]})
out = df.with_columns(
    via_eval=pl.col("a").list.eval(pl.element().null_count()),
    via_agg=pl.col("a").list.agg(pl.element().null_count()),
)
print(out.to_dict(as_series=False))
print(out.schema)
passed.output:
{'a': [[1, None], [42, 13], [None, None]], 'via_eval': [[1], [0], [2]], 'via_agg': [1, 0, 2]}
Schema({'a': List(Int64), 'via_eval': List(UInt32), 'via_agg': UInt32})

passed.title: Expr.list.explode turns empty and null lists into null rows
passed.trap: By default, `Expr.list.explode` uses `empty_as_null=True` and `keep_nulls=True`. An empty list and a null list each produce one null row instead of disappearing. Row counts and null counts after exploding are therefore higher than you might expect. Pass `empty_as_null=False` and `keep_nulls=False` to get only the actual elements.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[1, 2], [], None]})
default = df.select(pl.col("a").list.explode())
only_values = df.select(pl.col("a").list.explode(empty_as_null=False, keep_nulls=False))
print(default.to_dict(as_series=False))
print(default.height, only_values.height)
print(only_values.to_dict(as_series=False))

passed.title: Expr.list.item errors unless every sublist has exactly one value
passed.trap: `Expr.list.item` raises an error when any sublist does not have exactly one element. `allow_empty=True` only turns empty lists into null, and sublists with two or more elements still raise. Use `Expr.list.item` only when one element per list is a real invariant you want enforced. If you just want the leading value, use `Expr.list.first`.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[3, 2], [1], []]})
try:
    df.select(pl.col("a").list.item(allow_empty=True))
except Exception as e:
    print(getattr(type(e), "__name__"))
ok = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[7], []]})
print(ok.select(pl.col("a").list.item(allow_empty=True)).to_dict(as_series=False))
print(df.select(first=pl.col("a").list.first()).to_dict(as_series=False))
